transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I called EAP because lately every little bang at work makes me jump really hard. Like if a file drawer slams or someone drops a coffee mug, my chest starts racing, and it keeps going way longer than it should. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Can you think of any particular event or experience that might be connected to when these reactions to loud noises started?
Yeah. It started about two weeks ago, after this late-night confrontation I had with my regional boss. Since then, the noise reactions have been happening.
Can you tell me more about that late-night confrontation with your regional boss? Was it a particularly stressful or frightening experience for you?

I’m not really sure how to describe it. It was definitely tense, and it stuck with me, but I don’t know if I’d call it frightening exactly. It was late, I was tired, and the whole thing just felt… off. I’ve been trying to connect the dots, but I don’t have a clear answer beyond that.
Can you describe what happened during that late-night confrontation in more detail? Specifically, did you feel in danger or threatened in any way during the encounter?

I remember parts of it pretty clearly. He slammed a chair, and then he was standing in front of the door, which made me feel kind of trapped. But when I try to explain the worst part, like the actual words he said to me, it’s just blank. It’s like that section got cut out, and I can’t get it back clearly.
Is there any part of that confrontation that you just can’t remember, even though you know it happened?

Yeah. I remember him slamming the chair, and I remember him standing in front of the door. But the worst part—what he actually said to me—I just can’t pull it up. I know it happened, but it’s blank, like that part got cut out.
Since that confrontation with your boss, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or conversations because they remind you of that night?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding specific places or people because of it. I mean, I don’t like thinking about that night, but I can’t say I’ve been deliberately staying away from anything in particular.
Since that confrontation with your boss, have you had any sudden, intrusive memories or moments where you feel like you're re-experiencing parts of that night?
I don’t think so. I mean, I remember it when we talk about it or if I’m thinking about it, but I haven’t had moments where it suddenly feels like I’m back there or reliving it.
Since that confrontation with your boss, have you ever felt detached from yourself, like you were watching yourself from outside your body, or felt like the world around you seemed unreal?

Yeah, sometimes. Like during meetings, the room will start to feel kind of far away or unreal. I’ll be talking to my sales reps, but it feels like I’m watching myself do it instead of really being there.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself or like the world is unreal at times other than during meetings?

Not really outside of meetings, no. That’s the main time I’ve noticed it — I’ll be in the room talking to my sales reps, and it starts to feel distant or kind of unreal, like I’m watching myself instead of actually being there.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself or like the world is unreal at times other than during meetings?
No, not really outside of meetings. It’s mainly when I’m in there talking to my sales reps — the room kind of feels far away or unreal, like I’m watching myself instead of actually being there.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself or like the world was unreal in situations outside of your meetings with sales reps, even briefly?
I mean, not that I can really think of. It’s pretty much been in those meetings with the sales reps, where the room feels unreal and like I’m watching myself talk instead of being fully there.
Since that confrontation with your boss, have you been feeling ongoing fear, anger, or shame related to what happened that night?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve felt upset about it, but I don’t know if I’d call it ongoing fear or shame. It’s more just… I don’t like thinking about how it went.
Since that confrontation with your boss, have you ever felt detached from yourself or like the world was unreal even briefly, outside of your meetings with sales reps?

Not really outside of those meetings. It’s been more like, during the meetings, the room can start to feel far away or unreal, and I feel like I’m watching myself talk to the reps instead of really being there.
Since the confrontation with your boss, have you noticed any new physical symptoms like headaches, trouble sleeping, or stomach issues that seem related to your stress about that night?

I haven’t really noticed anything like that, no. I mean, I’ve been stressed thinking about it, but I can’t point to new headaches or stomach problems or sleep issues that clearly started because of that night.
Since the confrontation with your boss, have you felt a constant sense of anger, fear, or guilt that doesn’t seem to go away, even when you’re not thinking about that night?
No, I don’t think it’s constant like that. I get bothered when it comes up, but when I’m not thinking about it, I’m not walking around feeling angry or scared or guilty all the time.
Have you ever felt like things around you were unreal or that you were detached from yourself, even for a moment, when you weren’t in one of those meetings with your sales reps?
No, not really when I’m outside those meetings. It’s mainly in the meetings with the reps where the room feels kind of unreal or far away, like I’m watching myself talk instead of being fully there.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself or like the world was unreal when you were reminded of the confrontation with your boss, even if you weren't in a meeting?

Yeah, sometimes. It’s not really outside of those meetings, but when I’m in meetings with my sales reps, the room can start to feel far away or unreal. It’s like I’m watching myself talk instead of actually being fully there.

When you're reminded of the confrontation with your boss—like thinking about it or talking about it—do you ever feel detached from yourself or like the world is unreal, even for a moment, outside of your meetings with sales reps?

Not really outside of those meetings, no. When it happens, it’s usually during meetings with my sales reps—the room starts to feel kind of far away or unreal, like I’m watching myself talk instead of actually being there.
